clue.text: Where to begin trainspotting, free

indicators.note: letters set free from their order may be rearranged, so the long word is reshuffled

explanation.surface: Advice on how a newcomer should take up the hobby of noting train numbers, at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like an adjective about cost; it signals that TRAINSPOTTING is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A place from which you begin something is its starting point, a plain synonym phrase.

clue.text: Complaint of aunt finally in Austen novel

indicators.note: in places the last letter of aunt inside the novelist's name before it is shuffled
novel as an adjective means new or fresh, so the surname is given a new arrangement
finally points to the last letter of the word aunt

explanation.surface: Seems to ask which ailment a fictional aunt suffers in one of Jane Austen's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it is the anagram signal: T (the end of 'aunt') goes into AUSTEN and the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is a disease, and complaint is a standard word for an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Called for orange, peeled

indicators.note: a peeled fruit has lost its skin, so the word orange loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned asking for an orange with its skin removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Called on the telephone is the past tense synonym for having telephoned someone.

clue.text: Picture to hold in fancy

indicators.note: to hold means the first word wraps around and contains the second

parts.note: a picture is an image
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reads as a picture one keeps in one's daydreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' looks like the definition, which would also fit, but the verb here is 'fancy'; IMAGE holds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something, in the sense of supposing it, is to conjure it up in the mind.

clue.text: Refuse to boast about one's years

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for boasting is read backwards

parts.note: to boast is to brag
the number of years one has lived is one's age

explanation.surface: Someone declining to show off about how old they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish; 'about' turns BRAG into GARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is household rubbish, which Americans call trash.

clue.text: Simply unique

definitions.meaning: simply as in merely or just
unique as in the sole one of its kind

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as the adverb meaning merely and as the adjective meaning sole or single.

clue.text: Falls for a redhead once more, getting uplifted

indicators.note: in a down clue being lifted up means read from bottom to top, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: the head of the word red is its first letter
once more means again

explanation.surface: Someone falling in love with a red-haired person yet again and feeling elated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb about love; it is the waterfall. 'getting uplifted' turns A, R and AGAIN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border are known by this name.

clue.text: Where all the goods will be sold out

definitions.text: Where all the goods will be sold out

parts.words: Where all the goods will be sold out
parts.note: sold out reads as the stock running out, but here means sold outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: 'sold out' suggests a shop with no stock left; the trick is that the selling happens out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A street market with stalls under the sky sells its goods outside rather than indoors.

clue.text: Key point of a hotel?

parts.note: key point suggests the most important feature, but it is the place where guests collect their room keys

explanation.definitionFit: Hotel guests check in and receive their room keys at the front counter in the lobby.

clue.text: Tie up an unusually attractive plant

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an unexpected way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A gardener tying up a striking plant to a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourful bedding flower is a popular garden plant valued for its looks.

clue.text: Free delivery

definitions.meaning: free as a verb, to let go or liberate
delivery as in a liberation or a letting out, also a new record or film put out

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb meaning to set loose and the noun for a setting loose or issue.

clue.text: Women prepared to follow orders

parts.note: orders suggests commands, but it means religious orders that women join

explanation.definitionFit: Members of female religious communities belong to orders such as the Benedictines.

clue.text: The first to introduce the golden handshake?

definitions.text: The first to introduce the golden handshake?

parts.words: The first to introduce the golden handshake?
parts.note: a golden handshake is a large payoff, but here it is a touch that turns things to gold

explanation.walkthrough: A golden handshake is a generous severance payment; the mythical king of Phrygia turned everything he touched into gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek myth tells of a king whose touch turned all things, even food, to gold.

clue.text: Right time of life for passion

parts.note: a time or period of life is an age

explanation.surface: Suggests there is a proper age for falling in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce passion such as fury or violent anger is a synonym here.

clue.text: Fearful sort of weather?

definitions.meaning: in British slang, to be scared or nervous is to have the wind up

explanation.walkthrough: The scared sense is British informal usage, from 'get the wind up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both blustery, of weather, and nervous or frightened in British slang.

clue.text: Drives point home in essays

definitions.meaning: pushes a sharp point in, as with a knife
essays as a verb or noun meaning tries or attempts

explanation.surface: Someone presses their argument hard in their written compositions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essays' looks like written pieces; it means attempts, as in having a go.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means thrusts with a blade and also attempts, as in having a go at something.

clue.text: Fashionable church feature to give one an idea

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: A trendy piece of church architecture sparks a thought.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate a creative thought in someone is to motivate or stimulate them.

clue.text: Squeeze out just one more cent

parts.note: one more over the usual number is an extra
ct is the abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: A hard bargainer wringing one last penny out of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To press or draw something out forcibly, like juice from fruit, is the sense here.

clue.text: He's not content with scoring a bull

definitions.text: He's not content with scoring a bull

parts.words: He's not content with scoring a bull
parts.note: scoring a bull suggests darts, but here it means wounding a bull in the ring

explanation.walkthrough: A bull is a bullseye in darts; here it is a real animal, which the bullfighter must kill, not merely scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullfighter who delivers the final sword thrust in the ring is this figure.

clue.text: Its user may have to step on it to get through the work

definitions.text: Its user may have to step on it to get through the work

parts.words: Its user may have to step on it to get through the work
parts.note: step on it suggests hurrying, but it is literally a foot pressing a lever

explanation.walkthrough: 'step on it' is slang for hurry up; here the foot really presses down on a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Old sewing machines and spinning wheels are driven by a foot lever pressed up and down.

clue.text: In secrecy, cleverly reclaim materials

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: Describes a covert and ingenious recovery of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Processing used waste so it can be made into new things is reusing or reprocessing it.

clue.text: It doesn't allow English doctor on Greek ship

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A rule barring an English medic from sailing on a Greek vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ban on trade, which prohibits goods moving, is something that forbids or does not permit.

clue.text: Heart so affected, sounds can be heard within it

definitions.text: sounds can be heard within it

indicators.note: affected means altered or changed, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A heart so moved that its beats become audible.
explanation.definitionFit: The range within which a voice or noise is audible is a hearing distance.

clue.text: Flight departure

definitions.meaning: flight as in running away from danger
departure as in a withdrawal or going away

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an army's withdrawal or fleeing, and a quiet going away to a secluded place.

clue.text: Highlanders may do so even when sober

definitions.text: Highlanders may do so even when sober

parts.words: Highlanders may do so even when sober
parts.note: suggests staggering drunkenly, but it is the lively Scottish dance

explanation.walkthrough: The word means to stagger, as a drunk does, and is also a brisk Scottish folk dance, which Highlanders dance sober.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Scottish country dance shares its name with the verb for lurching unsteadily.

clue.text: Some players make it, others read it

definitions.meaning: sports players make points or goals

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the tally of points in a game and the written notation of a musical work.

clue.text: The poker-players' boss?

parts.note: boss suggests a person in charge, but it means a knob or raised ..., and also names a poker variant

explanation.walkthrough: A boss is also a raised knob; the same word as that knob names a form of poker with some cards dealt face up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an ornamental knob, as a boss is, and names a well-known poker game.

clue.text: Surrounded by a shadowy reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: shadowy means dim

explanation.surface: Something enveloped by a faint mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning in the middle of or among, as in standing among a crowd.

clue.text: Laid out in Salvador

indicators.note: laid out suggests arranged differently, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something set down in El Salvador or the Brazilian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salvador' looks like a place, but it is the first name of the surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish surrealist painter famous for melting clocks had this first name.

clue.text: Sort of disease treated by district nurses?

definitions.text: Sort of disease treated by district nurses?

parts.words: Sort of disease treated by district nurses?
parts.note: district nurses are community nurses, but here they treat illness native to a district

explanation.walkthrough: District nurses are British community nurses who visit patients at home; the clue jokes that they treat diseases peculiar to a district.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease regularly found among people of a particular region is described this way.

clue.text: Hail falling in layers in upper parts

definitions.text: Hail falling in layers in upper parts

parts.words: Hail falling in layers in upper parts
parts.note: hail suggests ice from the sky, but it also hints at an exclamation, and the sky is pictured as stacked layers

explanation.walkthrough: The sky was once pictured as stacked layers, as in seventh heaven; the word is also an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The sky or firmament, thought of as several layers above the earth, is meant here.

clue.text: Racehorse that's sure to have the most life, paradoxically

definitions.text: Racehorse that's sure to have the most life, paradoxically

parts.words: Racehorse that's sure to have the most life, paradoxically
parts.note: a lifeless horse sounds hopeless, yet the phrase means a certain winner

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase begins with a word meaning lifeless, yet names a sure winner, hence 'paradoxically'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or outcome considered completely certain to win is described by this idiom.
